scope: Twenty selected actual-content guides with specifically scoped credited pictures.

profiles.name: Cayuga
remainingGaps: Read stronger independent historical work on Cayuga homelands, displacement and distinct New York, Ontario and Oklahoma contexts.
Resolve identified factual-quality problems in the legacy history page without assuming that one present institution represents all Cayuga people.
The 2014 newsletter’s council perspective and programme plans must remain dated; current operation and competing authority are unassessed.

profiles.name: Cochiti Pueblo
remainingGaps: Read fuller Pueblo-published history and actual historical records before extending the short colonial chronology.
The scanned legislative handout and Federal Register notice remain unread leads, not completed source reviews.
Review dated educational evaluations before making claims about participation or language outcomes.

profiles.name: Havasupai
remainingGaps: Read community-published histories and underlying twentieth-century land-return records more fully.
Personal recollections remain attributed; no current territorial, health or visitor-access determination is made.
The USGS report’s later detailed cultural sections, figures and appendices were not reviewed.

profiles.name: Hopi
remainingGaps: Read village-specific and Tribal-government publications alongside these nonprofit perspectives.
Inspect underlying artist biographies and selected public programme evaluations.
The historical photograph is not a present-day portrait of all Hopi villages; no ceremonial imagery is reproduced.

profiles.name: Houlton Band of Maliseet
remainingGaps: Read original organizing and recognition records alongside the Band’s historical introduction.
Inspect substantive public dictionaries and community language materials individually; retain access and cultural limits.
The Meduxnekeag bridge photograph is modern regional infrastructure, not a Native-made cultural object or a reservation boundary.

profiles.name: Hualapai
remainingGaps: Read original litigation records and fuller Hualapai-authored histories before extending legal claims.
The linked master-plan report remains unread because its URL delivered a file-service shell.
Use dated Tribal publications for current figures, offices or programme outcomes.

profiles.name: Isleta Pueblo
remainingGaps: Read fuller Pueblo-published history and underlying archival records.
Isleta New Mexico and Ysleta del Sur Texas require separate community histories.
Confirm dated programme information and outcomes; no current schedule or language statistic is adopted.

profiles.name: Mashantucket Pequot
remainingGaps: Add original historical records and community-directed scholarship across different periods.
Review selected public museum resources individually; institutional access is not blanket permission to reproduce collections.

profiles.name: Massachusett
remainingGaps: Add selected original records and community-directed scholarship about Neponset and Ponkapoag.
Review other individually named Massachusett communities separately rather than treating linguistic, historical and present government categories as interchangeable.

profiles.name: Mohawk
remainingGaps: Develop separately verified starting paths for individual Mohawk communities and their different governing institutions.
Read community-specific historical and original boundary records before adding detailed chronology or present jurisdiction claims.
The modern Cornwall–Akwesasne bridge photograph illustrates a named river setting, not all Mohawk people or a territorial boundary.

profiles.name: Mohegan
remainingGaps: Read selected public Mohegan historical and language works across additional periods.
Inspect original institutional records where appropriate, without treating public museum descriptions as permissions for private cultural material.

profiles.name: Narragansett
remainingGaps: Review original colonial, state and community records and named scholarship before extending precise chronology or legal claims.
Inspect appropriate public language and institutional resources without disclosing culturally sensitive locations.

profiles.name: Nipmuc
remainingGaps: Seek additional directly attributed community histories and inspect original records behind historical claims.
Current leadership and recognition disputes remain outside this guide; do not adopt faction allegations or infer affiliation from shared names.

profiles.name: Oneida
remainingGaps: Inspect substantive New York Oneida Indian Nation publications beyond the existing navigation index.
Review original relocation and land-purchase records alongside separately scoped community accounts.
The museum place reference was inspected only in its indexed opening; no full-source count or exact former-village claim is made.

profiles.name: Onondaga
remainingGaps: Add separately verified Onondaga community and governmental contexts beyond this New York institutional focus.
Read historical records alongside community accounts without assigning an unsupported founding date.
A December 2008 lake view is dated regional imagery, not evidence of present water quality, restoration or boundaries.

profiles.name: Passamaquoddy
remainingGaps: Develop independently verified individual-community routes, using exact names, supported aliases and deduplication.
Inspect community-authored historical scholarship, original records and modern dictionary work before extending the chronology.
The supplied island picture is a modern place view, not a reconstruction of 1604, a living-village portrait or a legal boundary.

profiles.name: Seneca
remainingGaps: Develop separately verified Tonawanda and other Seneca community/government reading paths.
Inspect original historical and archival works alongside these government and institutional introductions.
The 2011 museum exterior is a dated whole-building photograph; artwork and collection-object rights are not separately inferred.

profiles.name: Tuscarora
remainingGaps: Compare North Carolina and northern Tuscarora histories with original records and separately verified community publications.
Detailed claims in the inherited North Carolina chronology remain unverified and are excluded from substantive counts.
The Neuse River photograph is a modern regional waterway view, not an exact village, present boundary or New York Nation territory.

profiles.name: Wampanoag
remainingGaps: Expand community-led starting routes across additional Wampanoag communities and governments.
Read underlying public records and individual museum/archive resources within their access and cultural protocols; no blanket reuse or title claim follows from a link.

profiles.name: Zuni
remainingGaps: Read fuller Zuni-authored history and appropriately public archival records.
Museum and tourism websites had SSL/time-out limits; the Nation-hosted 2021 feature supplied the inspected community account.
Compare differing excavation chronologies against original records before asserting a start year.
No ceremonial material, collection image or current visitor permission is supplied.

sourceCounting: 46 appended profile-source contexts and 32 same-ID/same-URL card updates, including explicit excluded/supporting metadata corrections. Shared/reused publications are not globally new works. Identity-only evidence excluded.
provenance: Selected scopes/dates and media-specific creator/source/rights/complete-available-frame limits retained. No private files or full third-party texts published.
